questions.question: What is the numerical value of (sin 30 deg + cos 60 deg)?
questions.explanation: sin 30 deg = 1/2 and cos 60 deg = 1/2. Therefore, sin 30 deg + cos 60 deg = 1/2 + 1/2 = 1.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 8, Section 8.3, Table 8.1

questions.question: Which of the following identities is correct for all acute angles theta?
questions.explanation: The three fundamental Pythagorean identities are: (1) sin^2(theta) + cos^2(theta) = 1, (2) 1 + tan^2(theta) = sec^2(theta), and (3) 1 + cot^2(theta) = cosec^2(theta).
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 8, Section 8.4

questions.question: What is the value of 9 sec^2 A - 9 tan^2 A?
questions.explanation: 9 sec^2 A - 9 tan^2 A = 9(sec^2 A - tan^2 A). Since sec^2 A - tan^2 A = 1, 9 * 1 = 9.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 8, Exercise 8.4 Question 4(i)

questions.question: Given 15 cot A = 8, what is the value of sin A?
questions.explanation: cot A = 8/15 = adjacent / opposite. Hypotenuse = sqrt(8^2 + 15^2) = sqrt(64 + 225) = sqrt(289) = 17. Therefore, sin A = opposite / hypotenuse = 15/17.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 8, Exercise 8.1 Question 4

questions.question: Evaluate: 2 tan^2 45 deg + cos^2 30 deg - sin^2 60 deg.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 8, Exercise 8.2 Question 1(ii)

questions.question: What is the simplified form of (sec A + tan A)(1 - sin A)?
questions.explanation: (1/cos A + sin A/cos A)(1 - sin A) = [(1 + sin A)/cos A] * (1 - sin A) = (1 - sin^2 A) / cos A = cos^2 A / cos A = cos A.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 8, Exercise 8.4 Question 4(iii)

questions.question: What is (1 + tan^2 A) / (1 + cot^2 A) equal to?
questions.explanation: (1 + tan^2 A) / (1 + cot^2 A) = sec^2 A / cosec^2 A = (1/cos^2 A) / (1/sin^2 A) = sin^2 A / cos^2 A = tan^2 A.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 8, Exercise 8.4 Question 4(iv)

questions.subtopic: Angle Calculation from Sum and Difference
questions.question: If tan(A + B) = sqrt(3) and tan(A - B) = 1/sqrt(3), where 0 deg < A + B <= 90 deg and A > B, find A and B.
questions.explanation: tan(A + B) = sqrt(3) => A + B = 60 deg. tan(A - B) = 1/sqrt(3) => A - B = 30 deg. Adding equations: 2A = 90 deg => A = 45 deg. Then B = 60 - 45 = 15 deg.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 8, Exercise 8.2 Question 3

questions.question: In triangle ABC right-angled at B, AB = 24 cm and BC = 7 cm. What is the value of sin A and cos A?
questions.explanation: AC = sqrt(24^2 + 7^2) = sqrt(576 + 49) = sqrt(625) = 25 cm. For angle A, opposite side = BC = 7 cm, adjacent = AB = 24 cm, hypotenuse = 25 cm. sin A = 7/25, cos A = 24/25.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 8, Exercise 8.1 Question 1

questions.question: What is the value of (2 tan 30 deg) / (1 + tan^2 30 deg)?
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 8, Exercise 8.2 Question 2(i)

questions.question: What is the value of (1 - tan^2 45 deg) / (1 + tan^2 45 deg)?
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 8, Exercise 8.2 Question 2(ii)

questions.subtopic: Maximum Value of Sine and Cosine
questions.question: For any acute angle theta (0 deg <= theta <= 90 deg), what is the maximum possible value of sin theta and cos theta?
questions.explanation: In any right triangle, hypotenuse is the longest side. Since sin theta = opposite/hypotenuse <= 1 and cos theta = adjacent/hypotenuse <= 1, their maximum value is 1 (occurring at 90 deg and 0 deg respectively).
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 8, Section 8.3

questions.question: What is sqrt((1 + sin A) / (1 - sin A)) equal to?
questions.explanation: Multiply numerator and denominator inside root by (1 + sin A): sqrt[(1 + sin A)^2 / (1 - sin^2 A)] = sqrt[(1 + sin A)^2 / cos^2 A] = (1 + sin A) / cos A = 1/cos A + sin A/cos A = sec A + tan A.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 8, Exercise 8.4 Question 5(vi)

questions.question: Simplify the expression: (cosec theta - cot theta)^2.
questions.explanation: (1/sin theta - cos theta/sin theta)^2 = (1 - cos theta)^2 / sin^2 theta = (1 - cos theta)^2 / (1 - cos^2 theta) = (1 - cos theta)^2 / [(1 - cos theta)(1 + cos theta)] = (1 - cos theta) / (1 + cos theta).
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 8, Exercise 8.4 Question 5(i)

questions.subtopic: Value of Equal Sine and Cosine
questions.question: For what acute angle theta is sin theta = cos theta?
questions.explanation: sin theta = cos theta => sin theta / cos theta = 1 => tan theta = 1. Since tan 45 deg = 1, theta = 45 deg.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 8, Section 8.3

questions.question: Express tan A in terms of sec A (where A is an acute angle):
questions.explanation: From 1 + tan^2 A = sec^2 A, tan^2 A = sec^2 A - 1 => tan A = sqrt(sec^2 A - 1).
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 8, Section 8.4, Example 12

questions.question: Evaluate: (5 cos^2 60 deg + 4 sec^2 30 deg - tan^2 45 deg) / (sin^2 30 deg + cos^2 30 deg).
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 8, Exercise 8.2 Question 1(v)

questions.question: What is the value of (tan theta * cot theta)?
questions.explanation: cot theta = 1 / tan theta. Therefore tan theta * cot theta = tan theta * (1/tan theta) = 1.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 8, Section 8.1

questions.question: Which of the following trigonometric ratios is NOT defined (tends to infinity)?
questions.explanation: tan 90 deg = sin 90 / cos 90 = 1/0 (not defined). sec 90 deg = 1 / cos 90 = 1/0 (not defined).
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 8, Section 8.3, Table 8.1

questions.question: In right triangle ABC right-angled at B, angle C = 30 deg and AB = 5 cm. What is the length of hypotenuse AC?
questions.explanation: sin C = AB / AC => sin 30 deg = 5 / AC => 1/2 = 5 / AC => AC = 5 * 2 = 10 cm.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 8, Section 8.3, Example 7
